feedback.selected: Bayes’ Rule calculates the probability of the evidence occurring regardless of the hypothesis.
feedback.answer: Bayes’ Rule updates the probability of a hypothesis (e.g., the coin being fair) by dividing the likelihood of the observed evidence given that hypothesis times the prior probability of the hypothesis by the overall probability of the evidence.
feedback.explanation: The lecture shows the formula P(fair|H)=P(H|fair)P(fair)/[P(H|fair)P(fair)+P(H|biased)P(biased)], illustrating how the prior and likelihood combine to give the posterior.
feedback.rationale: This ignores the division by the total evidence probability, which is essential.
